questions.question: Which of the following best describes how modern historians treat the Arabic chroniclers' figures for the size of Mansa Musa's Hajj caravan?
options: They treat the figures as rhetorical rather than statistical.
They consider the figures precise and reliable.
They believe the figures understate the caravan's true size.
They use the figures to calculate Musa's exact wealth.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Arabic chroniclers give widely varying figures and that modern historians treat these numbers as rhetorical rather than statistical.
Incorrect. The article explicitly says modern historians do not treat these figures as precise or reliable.
Incorrect. The article does not suggest the figures understate the caravan's size; it describes them as rhetorical.
Incorrect. The article does not link these figures to calculating Musa's exact wealth; it notes Time magazine said no accurate number can be put on his wealth.

questions.question: Based on the article, what best explains why Mansa Musa is relatively absent from Mandinka oral traditions compared to his predecessors?
options: Hostility toward his branch of the Keita dynasty may explain his scathing treatment or absence in oral histories.
He was not considered a legitimate ruler by the jeliw.
His reign was too short to be remembered by oral tradition.
Oral traditions focused exclusively on his Hajj rather than his rule.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that hostility towards Musa's branch of the Keita dynasty would explain his relative absence from or scathing treatment by oral histories.
Incorrect. While some historians cast doubt on his accession, the article does not say oral tradition excluded him because he was considered illegitimate.
Incorrect. The article describes his reign as long and significant, not too short to be remembered.
Incorrect. The article says oral tradition includes relatively little about Musa overall, not that it focused exclusively on his Hajj.

questions.question: Which inference about Mansa Musa's early reign is best supported by the article?
options: His early reign involved continuous military conflict with neighboring non-Muslim societies.
He spent his early reign primarily building mosques in Timbuktu.
He avoided military action to focus on preparing for his Hajj.
He delegated all military matters to his son Muhammad.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Musa's early reign was spent in continuous military conflict with neighboring non-Muslim societies.
Incorrect. The article associates mosque construction with his later reign, not his early reign.
Incorrect. The article says he likely spent much of his early reign preparing for the Hajj, but also emphasizes continuous military conflict, not avoidance of it.
Incorrect. The article says he left his son Muhammad to rule during the Hajj, not that Muhammad handled military matters during the early reign.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains the significance of copper in the Mali Empire according to the article?
options: Copper was incredibly scarce and prized, exchanged for gold at rates considered unfair by present-day standards.
Copper was the primary source of Mali's wealth, surpassing gold.
Copper was abundant and used to mint currency throughout the empire.
Copper was imported from Europe in exchange for salt.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that copper was incredibly scarce and prized in Sub-Saharan Africa and was exchanged for gold at rates considered unfair by present-day standards.
Incorrect. The article identifies gold, not copper, as the principal source of Mali's wealth.
Incorrect. The article describes copper as scarce, not abundant, and does not mention currency minting.
Incorrect. The article does not mention copper being imported from Europe or exchanged for salt.

questions.question: According to the article, what was one consequence of Mansa Musa's lavish spending in Cairo during his Hajj?
options: His gift-giving noticeably affected the value of gold in Egypt.
The Mamluk sultan imprisoned him for destabilizing the economy.
He ran out of gold before reaching Mecca.
Cairo's merchants refused to accept Malian gold.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that his lavish gift-giving in Cairo is said to have noticeably affected the value of gold in Egypt.
Incorrect. The article says the two rulers got along well and exchanged gifts; there is no mention of imprisonment.
Incorrect. The article says he ran out of money on the return journey near Suez, not before reaching Mecca.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Cairo merchants refusing Malian gold.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the article's assessment of the claim that Abu Ishaq al-Sahili designed the Djinguereber Mosque?
options: Subsequent scholarship has substantially qualified this attribution.
The article confirms al-Sahili was the principal designer.
The article states al-Sahili had no role in any construction in Mali.
The article says the mosque was built entirely by local Malian architects.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that subsequent scholarship has substantially qualified the attribution of the Djinguereber Mosque to al-Sahili.
Incorrect. The article says the attribution has been qualified, not confirmed.
Incorrect. The article says a royal audience chamber is firmly attributable to al-Sahili, so he did have some role.
Incorrect. The article mentions architects from Andalusia and Cairo in the tradition, not exclusively local Malian architects.

questions.question: According to the article, what does the name 'Kanku Musa' mean in MandÃ© tradition?
options: 'Musa, son of Kanku'.
'Musa, the wealthy ruler'.
'Musa, son of Abu Bakr'.
'Musa, the Hajji'.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that in MandÃ© tradition, Kanku Musa means 'Musa, son of Kanku', prefixing the mother's name.
Incorrect. The article does not translate Kanku Musa as 'Musa, the wealthy ruler'.
Incorrect. 'Musa ibn Abi Bakr' is a different name given by Arabic sources, not the meaning of Kanku Musa.
Incorrect. The title Hajji is separate from the name Kanku Musa.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the article describes the gold carried by camels on Musa's Hajj as an upper-bound literary topos rather than a measurement?
options: The figures reflect the absence of any audited contemporary count.
Modern historians have weighed the camels and confirmed the range.
Arabic chroniclers agreed on a single exact figure.
The camels carried only gold bars, not gold dust.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states the 23â136 kg range reflects the absence of any audited contemporary count and is treated as an upper-bound literary topos rather than a measurement.
Incorrect. The article does not say modern historians confirmed the range by weighing camels.
Incorrect. The article says the figures are widely varying, not that chroniclers agreed on a single exact figure.
Incorrect. The article says camels carried gold dust, not only gold bars.

questions.question: Based on the article, which of the following best characterizes the lineage debate surrounding Mansa Musa's parentage?
options: Sources conflict over whether his father was Faga Leye, Abu Bakr, or another ancestor, with some suggesting succession through the female line.
All sources agree his father was Sunjata.
Oral tradition clearly records his mother as Kanku and his father as Faga Leye without dispute.
Ibn Khaldun and Ibn Battuta provide identical accounts of his parentage.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article presents conflicting accounts: Niane says his father was Faga Leye, Ibn Khaldun calls him Musa ibn Abu Bakr, and Ibn Battuta names his grandfather Sariq Jata, leading to theories about succession through the female line.
Incorrect. The article does not say all sources agree his father was Sunjata; in fact, Sunjata is described as his great-uncle.
Incorrect. The article notes uncertainty, stating it is unclear whether the genealogy implied by Kanku Musa is literal, and Ibn Khaldun does not mention Faga Leye.
Incorrect. The article highlights differences between Ibn Khaldun and Ibn Battuta, not identical accounts.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why some modern historians doubt Mansa Musa's own account of how he came to power?
options: They suggest he may have deposed his predecessor and devised the voyage story to explain his accession.
Historical records prove his predecessor never launched any Atlantic expeditions.
His predecessor's fleet of 2,000 ships was discovered off the coast of Mali.
Ibn Khaldun documented that Musa seized power by force.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that some modern historians have cast doubt on Musa's version, suggesting he may have deposed his predecessor and devised the story about the voyage.
Incorrect. The article does not say records prove the expeditions never happened; it says the possibility has been taken seriously by several historians.
Incorrect. The article does not mention any discovery of the predecessor's fleet.
Incorrect. The article does not state that Ibn Khaldun documented a forceful seizure of power.
